title: Quentin and the Regiment
premise: In the final winter of the Republic of Velden, Casper Voss works as a courier carrying sealed diplomatic codes for a government already negotiating its own surrender. When a census taker named Quentin Hale notices that her papers list a brother who died years ago, he covers for her — and in doing so becomes entangled in her mission to smuggle her family onto the last evacuation ship out of the capital. As the regime's agents close in and Casper discovers the codes she carries could expose the officials who sold the republic, she must decide between delivering justice outside the law and securing the single remaining berth on the ship — a berth she ultimately gives to Quentin's orphaned niece while staying behind to see the truth published. The novel ends with Casper escaping overland as the city falls, her name cleared by the very documents she refused to burn.
about_author: Hazel Fairweather is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing the letters of displaced families from collapsed European states. She writes historical fiction about ordinary people caught between paperwork and history.

chapters.title: The Weight of Sealed Paper
chapters.summary: Casper Voss delivers coded dispatches through a snowbound capital, invisible in her courier's grey coat. POV: Casper. The beat is quiet competence masking dread, as rumors of surrender circulate in the ministries she serves.

chapters.title: One Question Too Many
chapters.summary: Census taker Quentin Hale arrives at Casper's tenement and asks about the brother listed on her registration — a brother long dead, whose identity she uses. POV: Casper. The emotional beat is frozen terror, broken when Quentin quietly marks the entry 'verified' and leaves.

chapters.title: A Debt in Ink
chapters.summary: Casper confronts Quentin in a tea house to learn why he lied for a stranger. He reveals his own falsified records protecting his late sister's daughter, Nell. POV: Quentin. The beat is wary mutual recognition between two people fluent in forgery of the soul.

chapters.title: Manifest of the Meridian
chapters.summary: Casper learns the last diplomatic ship, the Meridian, will carry only forty civilian berths alongside fleeing officials. Her family of five has no place. POV: Casper. The beat is cold arithmetic — love measured in seats.

chapters.title: The Ministry of Last Things
chapters.summary: Quentin, processing death registrations for the collapsing state, glimpses an order listing who may board the Meridian — and who has paid for their places. POV: Quentin. The beat is disillusionment; the ledger of the dying is written in bribes.

chapters.title: Mother's Hands
chapters.summary: Casper visits her mother, a seamstress sewing burial shrouds for the coming siege, and cannot bring herself to explain the ship. POV: Casper. The beat is tender evasion, love expressed through mended coats and unspoken things.

chapters.title: Codes in the Lining
chapters.summary: Casper's handler gives her a final dispatch sewn into her coat lining — and hints it contains something worth more than diplomacy. POV: Casper. The beat is dawning suspicion that she carries not orders but evidence.

chapters.title: The Inspector's Visit
chapters.summary: Regime inspector Aldous Krein begins auditing census rolls, hunting irregularities — and Quentin's forged entries surface. POV: Quentin. The beat is tightening fear as bureaucratic menace acquires a face.

chapters.title: Nell's Map
chapters.summary: Nine-year-old Nell shows Quentin a map she draws of the harbor, having memorized which piers are guarded. POV: Quentin. The beat is fierce protectiveness sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: An Offer from Krein
chapters.summary: Krein offers Quentin immunity for naming every falsified record — including Casper's. POV: Quentin. The beat is temptation framed as duty, justice weaponized against mercy.

chapters.title: The Brother Who Died Twice
chapters.summary: Casper traces how her dead brother's identity was stolen years ago by a ministry clerk — one of the men now holding Meridian berths. POV: Casper. The beat is grief transmuted into purpose.

chapters.title: What the Codes Say
chapters.summary: With a sympathetic telegraph clerk, Casper partially deciphers her sealed dispatch: proof that ministers sold defense contracts to the invading power. POV: Casper. The beat is vertigo — she holds justice in her coat lining and no lawful way to use it.

chapters.title: A Printer Named Sova
chapters.summary: Casper seeks an underground printer willing to publish the evidence, finding an old radical working by candlelight. POV: Casper. The beat is cautious hope kindled in a basement.

chapters.title: Quentin's Choice
chapters.summary: Quentin submits his audit — omitting Casper's name and adding three names of his own choosing, including Krein's corrupt superior. POV: Quentin. The beat is quiet rebellion dressed as compliance.

chapters.title: Berth Thirty-Nine
chapters.summary: Through a bribe arranged with stolen funds, Casper secures one civilian berth aboard the Meridian. One. For five family members. POV: Casper. The beat is triumph curdling immediately into impossibility.

chapters.title: The Family Council
chapters.summary: Casper's mother refuses the berth outright; her younger brother Tomas claims it as the family's future. The argument fractures at the dinner table. POV: Casper. The beat is love turning cruel under scarcity.

chapters.title: Krein Closes In
chapters.summary: Krein cross-references shipping manifests and realizes a berth was bought with ministry money. He suspects Quentin. POV: Krein (antagonist POV). The beat is patient, predatory satisfaction.

chapters.title: Night at the Print Shop
chapters.summary: Sova begins setting type for the exposé; Casper stands watch and confesses her whole history of borrowed identities. POV: Casper. The beat is intimacy born of shared risk.

chapters.title: The Harbor at Low Tide
chapters.summary: Quentin and Nell scout the pier where the Meridian will dock, mapping the gap in patrols Nell spotted. POV: Quentin. The beat is fragile hope, a child's cleverness against an empire.

chapters.title: Tomas Disappears
chapters.summary: Tomas vanishes — conscripted by press gangs sweeping the docks. The berth question dissolves into a rescue. POV: Casper. The beat is panic outrunning grief.

chapters.title: Bargaining with the Press Gang
chapters.summary: Casper trades her brother's identity papers — her own protection — to free Tomas from the conscription roll. POV: Casper. The beat is sacrifice without ceremony; she erases herself to save him.

chapters.title: Nowhere on the Rolls
chapters.summary: Legally erased, Casper can no longer claim any berth, any ration, any existence. Quentin finds her sleeping in the print shop. POV: Quentin. The beat is devastating tenderness — he alone knows she exists.

chapters.title: Krein's Ledger
chapters.summary: Krein presents his findings to his superiors, offering to trade Quentin's arrest for a Meridian berth of his own. POV: Krein. The beat is corruption consuming even its beneficiaries.

chapters.title: The Proof Set in Type
chapters.summary: The exposé is printed: two hundred copies hidden in flour sacks. Sova warns distribution may cost lives. POV: Casper. The beat is solemn commitment — truth as contraband.

chapters.title: Arrest Warrant
chapters.summary: Soldiers come for Quentin at the census office; a colleague tips him off minutes ahead. He flees with Nell to Casper. POV: Quentin. The beat is the collapse of his careful, lawful life.

chapters.title: Three Fugitives
chapters.summary: Hiding in the shroud-maker's attic, the three form a plan: distribute the pamphlets, reach the Meridian, save someone. POV: Casper. The beat is found-family solidarity forged in hiding.

chapters.title: The Distribution
chapters.summary: Over two days, the pamphlets flood the ministries and barracks; soldiers waver, clerks whisper. The city begins to turn. POV: multiple, anchored in Casper. The beat is exhilaration — justice moving faster than the law.

chapters.title: Krein's Reckoning
chapters.summary: Exposed by the pamphlet, Krein's superiors discard him; he becomes a hunted man seeking revenge on the couriers who ruined him. POV: Krein. The beat is a predator turned desperate.

chapters.title: The Mother's Decision
chapters.summary: Casper's mother reveals she has secretly arranged passage for Tomas and Nell with fishermen, and demands Casper take the Meridian berth herself. POV: mother, briefly, then Casper. The beat is generational reversal — the protected becoming protector.

chapters.title: Refusal
chapters.summary: Casper refuses the berth and instead gives it formally to Nell, forging the documents in her dead brother's name one final time. POV: Casper. The beat is the theme made flesh: love against duty, identity surrendered willingly.

chapters.title: Krein at the Door
chapters.summary: Krein tracks them to the attic. A standoff in the stairwell ends when Quentin's former census colleagues, moved by the pamphlet, bar the soldiers' way. POV: Quentin. The beat is ordinary courage tipping the scale.

chapters.title: The Burning of the Census Hall
chapters.summary: Rioters burn the census hall, erasing the regime's paper power. Quentin watches his life's records go up in smoke and feels freed rather than ruined. POV: Quentin. The beat is liberation through loss.

chapters.title: Embarkation Eve
chapters.summary: The Meridian loads at dawn. Casper walks Nell and Tomas to the gangway through crowds and checkpoints. POV: Casper. The beat is heartbreak held steady by purpose.

chapters.title: The Last Berth
chapters.summary: At the gangway, a guard challenges Nell's papers; Casper vouches for her with the courier seal she should have surrendered. The children board. POV: Casper. The beat is the climax's first peak — the choice completed at gunpoint.

chapters.title: What Casper Carried
chapters.summary: Krein intercepts Casper on the quay, demanding the original cipher key. She gives him the decoy copy; Sova's people already hold the true plates. POV: Casper. The beat is outwitting the hunter with the truth itself.

chapters.title: The Ship Departs
chapters.summary: The Meridian pulls away. On deck, Nell presses her hand to the rail; on the quay, Casper mouths goodbye. POV: alternating Casper/Nell. The beat is grief and hope sailing in opposite directions.

chapters.title: The Long Road North
chapters.summary: Casper, Quentin, and her mother flee overland with refugee columns toward the neutral border, pursued by remnants of Krein's faction. POV: Casper. The beat is endurance — survival as its own quiet defiance.

chapters.title: Justice Outside the Law
chapters.summary: News reaches the road: the pamphlet's revelations have sparked tribunals in exile; the ministers are named, warrants issued. The law finally catches up to what Casper carried. POV: Quentin. The beat is vindication arriving late but arriving.

chapters.title: Crossing
chapters.summary: At the border pass, guards demand names. Casper gives her real name for the first time in the entire book — Voss, her own, spoken aloud. POV: Casper. The beat is identity reclaimed; the emotional summit.

chapters.title: Letters to the Meridian
chapters.summary: Months later, in exile, Casper and Quentin receive Nell's first letter. They marry quietly; Casper begins work documenting the fallen republic's true record. POV: Casper. The beat is resolution — love rooted, justice written down, the story handed forward.
